This is NOT verified legal compliance and NOT a substitute for review by qualified UK legal counsel. Scope: National("GB"). Every rule's action is a conservative, generic engineering policy, not a legal conclusion. This content will age — re-verify before relying on it. ENRICHED 2026-10-27: additional rules below were verified by retrieving the official legislation.gov.uk contents pages on 2026-10-27 (pages state they are up to date with changes known to be in force on or before 27 October 2026); snippets quote only the Act titles, chapter numbers and section headings actually retrieved. rules.source: UK GDPR + Data Protection Act 2018 — gives individuals rights over personal data (access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, objection, and rights around automated decision-making), broadly mirroring EU GDPR post-Brexit. Official text: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2018/12/contents

UK GDPR (retained EU law) — notification obligations to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) mirror the EU GDPR 72-hour breach-notification standard. Official text: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2018/12/contents

Public Sector Bodies (Websites and Mobile Applications) Accessibility Regulations 2018 — requires public sector websites/apps to meet WCAG 2.2 AA and publish an accessibility statement; in force since 23 September 2018 (websites) / 23 June 2021 (mobile apps). Scope: public sector bodies (central/local government, certain publicly-funded charities/NGOs), not general private-sector services. Official: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/accessibility-requirements-for-public-sector-websites-and-apps
rules.retrieved_snippet: The Public Sector Bodies (Websites and Mobile Applications) Accessibility Regulations of 2018 require public sector websites and mobile apps to meet WCAG 2.2 AA and publish an accessibility statement explaining how accessible their website or app is. Came into force 23 September 2018 for websites and 23 June 2021 for mobile applications.

Online Safety Act 2023, 2023 c. 50; legislation.gov.uk shows the Act as enacted and up to date with changes known to be in force on or before 27 October 2026 (some changes may take effect at a future date).

Computer Misuse Act 1990, 1990 c. 18. Section headings: s.1 'Unauthorised access to computer material'; s.2 'Unauthorised access with intent to commit or facilitate commission of further offences'; s.3 'Unauthorised acts with intent to impair, or with recklessness as to impairing, operation of computer, etc.'; s.3ZA 'Unauthorised acts causing, or creating risk of, serious damage'; s.3A 'Making, supplying or obtaining articles for use in offence under section 1, 3 or 3ZA'.

Equality Act 2010, 2010 c. 15. Section 4 'The protected characteristics' with ss.5-12 headed Age; Disability; Gender reassignment; Marriage and civil partnership; Race; Religion or belief; Sex; Sexual orientation.
Terrorism Act 2000, 2000 c. 11. Part I 'Introductory' with s.1 'Terrorism: interpretation'; under Part II offences, s.12 'Support'.

Consumer Rights Act 2015, 2015 c. 15. Part 1 'Consumer contracts for goods, digital content and services' with Chapter 1 Introduction, Chapter 2 Goods, Chapter 3 Digital content, Chapter 4 Services, Chapter 5 General and supplementary provisions.
Defamation Act 2013, 2013 c. 26. Section 1 is headed 'Serious harm'.
Gambling Act 2005, 2005 c. 19. Part 1 section 1 is headed 'The licensing objectives'.
Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988, 1988 c. 48. Part I 'Copyright' with s.1 'Copyright and copyright works.'
